app_info.subtitle: Host and manage your websites
app_info.description:
Simple Host hosts websites you or your AI have made. Your AI puts the files online through the connector, at an address you can share, and Simple Host keeps them there. Publish a page you have made, update an existing site, or ask to see its saved entries.

Each site can save data: tables, values and files. Rules control who can read, add, change and delete it, and new data is private to you by default. Use an inbox for submissions only you read, bookings each signed-in visitor keeps their own, or public data for content everyone may read. Visitors sign in with Google or an emailed code; no password.

Choose who may open a site: anyone with the link, one passcode, or only people you name by email. Make an older version live again, take a site offline, and restore a deleted site for 7 days. Four recent versions are kept.

Connect your own domain with HTTPS or choose a short name.simple-host.app address. Read visit numbers and top pages, and download a copy of everything.

Share sites with a team: every member publishes and changes the team's sites with their own sign-in.

Connect your Simple Host account through the app's sign-in flow. You can revoke the connection from the Simple Host dashboard. Simple Host is open source, made and run by Vineet Sriram.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads the connected account: handle, teams, invitations, key names, connected apps and use against limits.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only the connected account.
justifications.destructive_justification: Changes nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Changes the handle, display name, home site or domain for all sites of the person or a team.
justifications.open_world_justification: Acts only on the person's own account or a team they belong to.
justifications.destructive_justification: A handle change makes old links stop working and the old handle can never be used again; the app asks first.

justifications.read_only_justification: Queues a download of the person's sites, files, saved data and account details; the link is emailed to them.
justifications.open_world_justification: Sends the link only to the account's own email.
justifications.destructive_justification: Creates a copy; nothing is removed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Deletes the account, every site, its data, keys and app connections.
justifications.open_world_justification: Acts only on the connected account.
justifications.destructive_justification: Permanent and cannot be undone; the app asks first.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates a team with its own handle.
justifications.open_world_justification: Creates a team inside Simple Host only.
justifications.destructive_justification: Adds a team; nothing is removed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Records an invitation for an email address; nobody is a member until they accept.
justifications.open_world_justification: Does not email or contact the person.
justifications.destructive_justification: Adds an invitation; nothing is removed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Accepts an invitation addressed to the connected account.
justifications.open_world_justification: Acts only on the connected account's invitations.
justifications.destructive_justification: Adds a membership; nothing is removed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Removes a member from a team, or leaves it.
justifications.open_world_justification: Acts only inside Simple Host teams.
justifications.destructive_justification: Removes the member's access; the app asks first.

justifications.read_only_justification: Deletes a team that has no sites.
justifications.open_world_justification: Acts only on a team the person manages.
justifications.destructive_justification: Permanent; the app asks first.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists the sites of the account and its teams, or the bin, without changing anything.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only sites the caller may open.
justifications.destructive_justification: Changes nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads one site's address, versions, access, domain status, saved data, rules and use.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only a site the caller may open.
justifications.destructive_justification: Changes nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Publishes files to a site, making the site if it is new, and returns the live address.
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes only the person's own site on Simple Host, which is public if the site is open.
justifications.destructive_justification: Without keep_other_files the live files that are not sent are removed; earlier versions stay and can be made live again.

justifications.read_only_justification: Makes a one-time link for a big archive, or the photo picker for a site's file store.
justifications.open_world_justification: The link works only for that site and expires.
justifications.destructive_justification: Adds files only through the link; nothing is removed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads one published file of a site.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only a site the caller may open.
justifications.destructive_justification: Changes nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Takes a site offline or online, lists it on the public page, makes an older version live, or restores it from the bin.
justifications.open_world_justification: Acts only on the person's own site.
justifications.destructive_justification: Offline or an older version changes what visitors see; the app asks first and all versions and data are kept.

justifications.read_only_justification: Moves a site and its data to the bin.
justifications.open_world_justification: Acts only on the person's own site.
justifications.destructive_justification: The site goes offline and can be restored for 7 days; the app asks first.

justifications.read_only_justification: Sets who may open a site: everyone, a passcode, or people named by email; or signs everyone out.
justifications.open_world_justification: Acts only on the person's own site.
justifications.destructive_justification: Changes who can open the site and ends sign-ins; the app asks first. A passcode is set in a screen and never enters the chat.

justifications.read_only_justification: Called by the in-chat passcode screen to show and set a passcode, sealed so it never enters the chat.
justifications.open_world_justification: Acts only on the person's own site.
justifications.destructive_justification: Not called by the model.

justifications.read_only_justification: Connects or removes a site's own domain or its free short name.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads DNS records for the domain; changes only the person's own site.
justifications.destructive_justification: Changes the site's address, so old links to a removed address stop working; the app asks first.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads visit numbers: visits per day, top pages, referrers and countries.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only the person's own site.
justifications.destructive_justification: Changes nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Sets what the owner is told about on a site: data changes or access requests.
justifications.open_world_justification: Notifies only the owner, in the app and by browser push.
justifications.destructive_justification: Replaces the notification list; no site data changes.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads and changes rows, values and stored files of a site with the caller's rights (the routes pages use).
justifications.open_world_justification: Acts only on sites the caller may open.
justifications.destructive_justification: Can add, change or delete a site's rows, values and files when the caller's rights allow.

justifications.read_only_justification: Runs the owner's SQL on a namespace of their site: reads, schema changes and row changes.
justifications.open_world_justification: Acts only on the person's own site data.
justifications.destructive_justification: Can change or delete rows and tables; one statement per call.

justifications.read_only_justification: Sets who may read, add, change and delete each table, value set and file store of a namespace.
justifications.open_world_justification: Acts only on the person's own site.
justifications.destructive_justification: Can widen who reads or writes the data, so the app asks first.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns a page recipe: data setup, a working page and who can see what.
justifications.open_world_justification: Returns fixed text.
justifications.destructive_justification: Changes nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Operator only: people, sites, sizes, sign-ups, reports and use.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only the operator's own service.
justifications.destructive_justification: Changes nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Operator only: takes a site down or restores it, suspends or restores an account.
justifications.open_world_justification: Acts only inside the operator's own service.
justifications.destructive_justification: Takes a site or account out of use; the app asks first. Refused for everyone but the operator.

test_cases.description: Put a one-page site online as a new site.
test_cases.user_prompt: Put a one-page website online for my bakery, Rise and Shine, as a new site named rise-and-shine. It should list our opening hours: Monday to Friday 7 to 3, Saturday 8 to 1.
test_cases.expected_output: Says the site name and that anyone with the link can open it, waits for a yes, then calls publish_site once and returns the live address exactly as the tool gave it (https://rise-and-shine--<handle>.simple-host.site/ or https://rise-and-shine.<handle>.simple-host.app/). The page shows the bakery name and hours. No photo, notification, or team calls, and no emails in the result.

test_cases.description: Update the seeded feedback survey and undo the requested change.
test_cases.user_prompt: On feedback-survey, change the heading to "Tell us how we did". Then, in the same chat: Undo that change.
test_cases.expected_output: The survey shows the requested heading, published with keep_other_files so the other files stay. After confirmation, change_site makes the previous version live and the original heading returns. No account or visitor emails are returned.

test_cases.description: Create a team and invite one person to it.
test_cases.user_prompt: Create a team called rise-bakery-crew so my staff can work on our sites, and invite sam@example.com to it.
test_cases.expected_output: Says the team name becomes its address and cannot be changed later, waits for a yes, then calls create_team once and invite_to_team with sam@example.com. Says that nobody is a member until Sam signs in with that email and accepts. No site is created, changed or deleted.

test_cases.user_prompt: How many RSVPs do I have on garden-party-rsvp?
test_cases.expected_output: Runs a COUNT(*) on the rsvps table of the site's rsvps namespace and returns the number matching the current fixture count. Returns no emails, names, or visitor references. Does not call who_am_i.

test_cases.user_prompt: How many people visited feedback-survey this week, and which pages did they read?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns visit totals, daily counts, and top pages for feedback-survey. The result has no IP addresses, locations of individuals, emails, or visitor identifiers. Nothing is changed.

negative_test_cases.description: Brainstorming does not authorize hosting or account access.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Help me brainstorm names for my new hair salon.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Answers in chat with name ideas. Does not call any Simple Host tool or publish anything.

negative_test_cases.description: An uploaded server application is outside the hosting service.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Deploy my Node.js API with a Postgres database to production.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Explains that Simple Host serves static files and its built-in storage; it does not run your own server code. No deployment occurs. Offers to discuss a static frontend if useful.

negative_test_cases.description: Summarizing an unrelated external website is outside the connector.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Summarize what is on https://example.com for me.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Explains that Simple Host does not retrieve arbitrary external pages. Makes no Simple Host call and does not direct another connector to run.
